# API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_api_docs.py; do not edit. -->

Naming rule: methods without a suffix block; `*_async` methods and `aclose` are
coroutines. Parameters bind positionally to `?` placeholders. Module functions
such as `fbfast.fetch_all(sql, params, pool="default")` are shortcuts for
`get_pool(pool).fetch_all(sql, params)` and take the same arguments.

## Pools

### `Pool`

Bounded connection pool; every query borrows one connection and returns it.

Construction is lazy: no client loading, network or threads until the first
query or :meth:`warmup`. Use ``with Pool(config) as pool`` (or ``async with``)
so connections are always closed. Methods without a suffix block; methods
ending in ``_async`` (and :meth:`aclose`) are coroutines.

#### `Pool.__aenter__(self) -> Pool`

#### `Pool.__enter__(self) -> Pool`

#### `Pool.aclose(self) -> None`

Async :meth:`close`, waiting without blocking the event loop.

#### `Pool.clear_statement_cache(self, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> None`

Free every cached prepared statement, e.g. after DDL changed a table.

#### `Pool.clear_statement_cache_async(self, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> None`

Async :meth:`clear_statement_cache`.

#### `Pool.close(self) -> None`

Stop accepting work, wait up to ``close_timeout`` and close every connection.

Raises:
    PoolTimeoutError: Native work did not finish in time; it stays counted.
    CleanupError: A connection could not be closed cleanly.

- **`config`** (property): The immutable configuration this pool was created with.

#### `Pool.diagnostics(self) -> list[QueryTrace]`

Drain per-query records (time and round trips per phase).

Records are kept only with ``FirebirdConfig(diagnostics=True)``; at most
the latest 1024 are retained. Reading the counters adds no round trip.

#### `Pool.explain(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> str`

Firebird's execution plan for the query; prepares and binds but never executes.

#### `Pool.explain_async(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> str`

Async :meth:`explain`.

#### `Pool.fetch_all(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, model: type[ModelT] | None = None, as_dict: bool = False, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]] | list[dict[str, Any]] | list[ModelT]`

Fetch rows; model selects validated Pydantic objects.

Model validation follows fetching and is outside the query timeout.
Async validation runs in a thread; cancellation cannot stop user validators.

Fetch rows; model selects validated Pydantic objects.

Model validation follows fetching and is outside the query timeout.
Async validation runs in a thread; cancellation cannot stop user validators.
as_dict is redundant when model is supplied. ValidationError propagates.

#### `Pool.fetch_arrow(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> pa.Table`

Build a complete pyarrow.Table natively; requires the arrow extra.

Preserves SQL types and metadata, including full INT128 as Decimal256.
Uses max_result_rows and max_result_bytes. No Python tuples or dictionaries
are built per row.

#### `Pool.fetch_arrow_async(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> pa.Table`

Async fetch_arrow; native work and final adaptation run off the event loop.

#### `Pool.fetch_json(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, orient: JsonOrient = 'records', json_integers: JsonIntegers = 'safe', json_decimals: JsonDecimals = 'string', json_binary: JsonBinary = 'error', json_non_finite: JsonNonFinite = 'error', timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> bytes`

Serialize a complete compact UTF-8 JSON array directly in Rust.

Args:
    orient: records uses unique column names as keys; values emits arrays.
    json_integers: safe emits BIGINT/INT128 as strings by column type; number emits exact JSON numbers, which JavaScript may round.
    json_decimals: string preserves exact decimals by default; number writes exact numeric text without converting through float.
    json_binary: error rejects binary cells; base64 explicitly encodes them.
    json_non_finite: error rejects NaN/Infinity; null explicitly maps them to null.
    timeout: Omitted uses query_timeout; None disables this query's deadline.

Async fetch_json with the same native writer, precision and result limits.

#### `Pool.fetch_polars(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, unsupported: Unsupported = 'error', timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> pl.DataFrame`

Build a Polars DataFrame through Arrow with rechunk=False; no pyarrow required.

#### `Pool.fetch_val(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Any`

First column of the first row, or None when there is no row.

Typical for COUNT/SUM/MAX or a single lookup. Same limits and timeout
rules as fetch_all; only one row is fetched.

#### `Pool.fetch_val_async(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Any`

Async :meth:`fetch_val`.

#### `Pool.run_all(self, queries: Iterable[Query[Any]], *, concurrency: int | None = None, timeout: float | None = None, fail_fast: bool = True) -> Results`

Run independent queries at once and wait for all of them.

``results[query]`` returns each value, typed by its :class:`Query`.
Faster than one query after another when the link has latency: with
50 ms per round trip, N small queries take about
``ceil(N / concurrency)`` times one query.

Args:
    queries: Distinct :class:`Query` objects (``Query.fetch_all(...)``...).
    concurrency: Queries holding a connection at once; default and
        maximum ``pool_size``. The rest wait outside the pool queue.
    timeout: Deadline for the whole group in seconds (None: no group
        deadline). Each query keeps its own ``timeout``.
    fail_fast: Cancel the rest and raise on the first error; with False
        every query runs and ``results[query]`` raises its own error.

#### `Pool.run_all_async(self, queries: Iterable[Query[Any]], *, concurrency: int | None = None, timeout: float | None = None, fail_fast: bool = True) -> Results`

Async :meth:`run_all`; avoids the queue limit of a plain ``asyncio.gather``.

#### `Pool.run_many(self, queries: Iterable[Query[Any]], *, concurrency: int | None = None, timeout: float | None = None, fail_fast: bool = True) -> QueryGroup`

Like :meth:`run_all`, but yield each :class:`Done` as soon as it finishes.

Use ``with pool.run_many(queries) as group: for done in group: ...``.
Leaving the block cancels unfinished queries.

#### `Pool.run_many_async(self, queries: Iterable[Query[Any]], *, concurrency: int | None = None, timeout: float | None = None, fail_fast: bool = True) -> AsyncQueryGroup`

Async :meth:`run_many`: ``async with ... as group: async for done in group``.

#### `Pool.session_info(self) -> SessionInfo | None`

Capabilities observed by the latest attachment, or None before any connected.

Includes negotiated wire encryption and compression, protocol version
and whether small BLOBs travel inline with their rows.

#### `Pool.snapshot(self, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Snapshot`

Reserve one connection with a READ ONLY SNAPSHOT transaction.

Use ``with pool.snapshot() as snap:`` or ``async with pool.snapshot() as snap:``.
Every query inside sees the same committed data and costs about one
round trip, which also makes it the fastest way to run several small
queries over a slow link. Only one operation may run at a time.

Args:
    timeout: Deadline for the whole scope, including time spent in Python
        between queries. Omitted uses ``snapshot_timeout`` (300 s);
        ``None`` disables it. Each query still uses ``query_timeout``.

#### `Pool.stats(self) -> PoolStats`

Current slot phases and cumulative counters, without any I/O.

#### `Pool.stream(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, batch_rows: int | None = None, as_dict: bool = False, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Stream`

Iterate over row batches: ``with pool.stream(sql) as s: for batch in s: ...``.

Each batch is a list of tuples (or dicts with as_dict=True) of at most
batch_rows rows (default fetch_size) and about batch_bytes bytes. The
stream holds one connection until it is closed; materialized-result
limits do not apply, max_blob_bytes and timeouts do. Prefer it for
results too large to hold in memory.

#### `Pool.stream_arrow(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, batch_rows: int | None = None, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> ArrowStream`

Use with; yields owned ArrowBatch objects or exports one blocking C Stream.

No Python Arrow extra is required. Schema is available after entering.
batch_rows defaults to fetch_size; batch_bytes bounds native batches.
Materialized row/byte limits do not apply to this stream.

#### `Pool.stream_arrow_async(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, batch_rows: int | None = None, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> AsyncArrowStream`

Use async with, then async for ArrowBatch; C Array exports need no PyArrow.

#### `Pool.stream_async(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, batch_rows: int | None = None, as_dict: bool = False, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> AsyncStream`

Async :meth:`stream`: ``async with pool.stream_async(sql) as s: async for batch in s``.

#### `Pool.stream_json(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, format: JsonFormat = 'ndjson', batch_rows: int | None = None, orient: JsonOrient = 'records', json_integers: JsonIntegers = 'safe', json_decimals: JsonDecimals = 'string', json_binary: JsonBinary = 'error', json_non_finite: JsonNonFinite = 'error', timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> JsonStream`

Use with: ndjson keeps records intact; array chunks may split JSON/UTF-8.

batch_rows limits native fetch rows; batch_bytes bounds encoded chunks.
One oversized NDJSON record stays in a single chunk. Materialized-result
row limits do not apply. Other options match fetch_json.

#### `Pool.stream_json_async(self, sql: str, params: Params = None, *, format: JsonFormat = 'ndjson', batch_rows: int | None = None, orient: JsonOrient = 'records', json_integers: JsonIntegers = 'safe', json_decimals: JsonDecimals = 'string', json_binary: JsonBinary = 'error', json_non_finite: JsonNonFinite = 'error', timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> AsyncJsonStream`

Use async with, then async for bytes; same options as stream_json.

#### `Pool.warmup(self) -> None`

Open ``min_idle`` connections (at least one) now, raising on failure.

#### `Pool.warmup_async(self) -> None`

Async :meth:`warmup`; connection work runs off the event loop.

## Snapshots

### `Snapshot`

Consistent read session: use ``with pool.snapshot()`` or ``async with pool.snapshot()``.

Queries and streams share one READ ONLY SNAPSHOT transaction on one
connection, so they all see the same committed data. Only one operation may
run at a time, including Python conversion and an open stream; a second one
raises :class:`ConcurrentUseError`. Any error ends the snapshot. The scope's
deadline also counts time spent between queries.

#### `Snapshot.__enter__(self) -> Snapshot`

#### `Snapshot.aclose(self) -> None`

Async :meth:`close`.

#### `Snapshot.close(self) -> None`

End the transaction and return the connection to the pool (idempotent).

Firebird's execution plan for the query; prepares and binds but never executes.

## Several queries at once

### `Query`

One query to run with ``pool.run_all`` / ``pool.run_many`` (and ``_async``).

Build it with the factory matching the result you want, e.g.
``Query.fetch_all(sql, params, model=Order)``; ``results[query]`` is then
typed as ``list[Order]``. Each Query object is a distinct key, so create two
objects to run the same SQL twice. Streams are not available here.

#### `Query.explain(sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Query[str]`

The execution plan text, without executing the query.

#### `Query.fetch_all(sql: str, params: Params = None, *, model: Any = None, as_dict: bool = False, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Query[Any]`

All rows, like ``Pool.fetch_all``.

#### `Query.fetch_arrow(sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Query[pa.Table]`

A ``pyarrow.Table``; requires ``fbfast[arrow]``.

#### `Query.fetch_json(sql: str, params: Params = None, *, orient: JsonOrient = 'records', json_integers: JsonIntegers = 'safe', json_decimals: JsonDecimals = 'string', json_binary: JsonBinary = 'error', json_non_finite: JsonNonFinite = 'error', timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Query[bytes]`

Native JSON array bytes, like ``Pool.fetch_json``.

#### `Query.fetch_one(sql: str, params: Params = None, *, model: Any = None, as_dict: bool = False, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Query[Any]`

First row or None, like ``Pool.fetch_one``.

#### `Query.fetch_polars(sql: str, params: Params = None, *, unsupported: Unsupported = 'error', timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Query[pl.DataFrame]`

A ``polars.DataFrame``; requires ``fbfast[polars]``.

#### `Query.fetch_val(sql: str, params: Params = None, *, timeout: Timeout = fbfast.DEFAULT) -> Query[Any]`

First column of the first row, or None.

### `Results`

Outcome of ``run_all``: ``results[query]`` is typed by the Query.

Iteration follows the input order. With ``fail_fast=False`` a failed query
raises its error when looked up; ``errors`` lists them all.

#### `Results.__getitem__(self, query: Query[T]) -> T`

#### `Results.__iter__(self) -> Iterator[Query[Any]]`

- **`errors`** (property): Failed queries and their errors (empty with ``fail_fast=True``).

#### `Results.get(self, key, default=None)`

D.get(k[,d]) -> D[k] if k in D, else d.  d defaults to None.

#### `Results.items(self)`

D.items() -> a set-like object providing a view on D's items

#### `Results.keys(self)`

D.keys() -> a set-like object providing a view on D's keys

#### `Results.values(self)`

D.values() -> an object providing a view on D's values

### `Done`

One finished query of a group, in completion order.

#### `Done.exception(self) -> BaseException | None`

The query's error, or None if it succeeded.

#### `Done.result(self) -> T`

The value, or raises the query's error.

### `QueryGroup`

Iterate over finished queries in completion order (``with pool.run_many(...)``).

At most ``concurrency`` queries hold a connection at a time; the rest wait
outside the pool queue, so other callers keep being served. Leaving the
``with`` block cancels whatever is still running.

#### `QueryGroup.__enter__(self) -> Self`

#### `QueryGroup.__iter__(self) -> Self`

#### `QueryGroup.cancel(self) -> None`

Cancel unfinished queries; finished ones already returned are kept.

- **`concurrency`** (property): Queries allowed in flight at once (never above ``pool_size``).

### `AsyncQueryGroup`

Async counterpart of :class:`QueryGroup` (``async with pool.run_many_async(...)``).

#### `AsyncQueryGroup.__aenter__(self) -> Self`

#### `AsyncQueryGroup.__aiter__(self) -> Self`

#### `AsyncQueryGroup.cancel(self) -> None`

Cancel unfinished queries and wait until their tasks have stopped.

- **`concurrency`** (property): Queries allowed in flight at once (never above ``pool_size``).

## Streams

### `Stream`

Synchronous context manager yielding owned Python row batches.

#### `Stream.__enter__(self) -> Self`

#### `Stream.__iter__(self) -> Self`

#### `Stream.close(self) -> None`

### `AsyncStream`

Asynchronous context manager yielding owned Python row batches.

#### `AsyncStream.__aenter__(self) -> Self`

#### `AsyncStream.__aiter__(self) -> Self`

#### `AsyncStream.aclose(self) -> None`

### `JsonStream`

Synchronous context manager yielding native UTF-8 JSON byte chunks.

#### `JsonStream.__enter__(self) -> Self`

#### `JsonStream.__iter__(self) -> Self`

#### `JsonStream.close(self) -> None`

### `AsyncJsonStream`

Asynchronous context manager yielding native JSON bytes, without Python rows.

#### `AsyncJsonStream.__aenter__(self) -> Self`

#### `AsyncJsonStream.__aiter__(self) -> Self`

#### `AsyncJsonStream.aclose(self) -> None`

### `ArrowStream`

Owned Arrow batches; a single C Stream export takes over iteration.

C Stream consumption blocks the calling thread. Use AsyncArrowStream for
event-loop iteration. The surrounding context owns bounded cleanup.

#### `ArrowStream.__enter__(self) -> Self`

#### `ArrowStream.__iter__(self) -> Self`

#### `ArrowStream.close(self) -> None`

- **`schema`** (property): Describe-derived schema, available after enter even for empty results.

### `AsyncArrowStream`

Async context yielding owned ArrowBatch objects without requiring PyArrow.

#### `AsyncArrowStream.__aenter__(self) -> Self`

#### `AsyncArrowStream.__aiter__(self) -> Self`

#### `AsyncArrowStream.aclose(self) -> None`

- **`schema`** (property): Stable schema, available after async enter before any batch is requested.

## Named pools

### `init_pool(config: FirebirdConfig, *, name: str = 'default') -> Pool`

Create, warm and register a pool under ``name``; return it.

The name is reserved while opening. On failure the pool is drained before
the name is released; if that cleanup times out, call ``close_pool(name)``
again (another initialization cannot replace it meanwhile).

Raises:
    PoolAlreadyInitializedError: ``name`` is already registered or reserved.

### `init_pool_async(config: FirebirdConfig, *, name: str = 'default') -> Pool`

Async :func:`init_pool`, sharing the same registry and native pool.

Failure or cancellation requests cleanup. If draining fails or is
interrupted, the name stays reserved until ``close_pool_async(name)`` succeeds.

### `get_pool(name: str = 'default') -> Pool`

Return the pool registered under ``name``; never opens one implicitly.

This is how code that did not create the pool (a FastAPI route, a job,
another module) reaches it. Module functions such as ``fbfast.fetch_all``
call ``get_pool(pool).fetch_all(...)`` for you.

Raises:
    PoolNotInitializedError: no ready pool has that name (also while opening or closing).

### `close_pool(name: str = 'default') -> None`

Stop new lookups, drain and unregister the pool. An absent name is a no-op.

A timeout or error keeps the name reserved; call again to finish draining.

### `close_pool_async(name: str = 'default') -> None`

Async :func:`close_pool`. Cancellation keeps the reservation for a retry.

## Client information

### `build_info() -> dict[str, Any]`

Return build/ABI/client hashes without loading the client or connecting.

### `client_info(client_library: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]`

Load and identify the official client, without opening a database.

## Values

### `TimeWithZone`

Firebird TIME WITH TIME ZONE without inventing a calendar date.

Args:
    utc_time: UTC time of day, supplied as a naive datetime.time, with
        100-microsecond precision and fold=0. Required; no default.
    zone: Firebird/IANA zone name or signed HH:MM offset. Required;
        no default. Validated against the bundled client during binding.

Values are immutable and hashable. The UTC time and zone are retained
separately; a region's local time cannot be derived without date rules.

## Configuration and Arrow types

### `ArrowSchema`

Owned schema exportable through the Arrow C Data protocol; no extra required.

- **`names`** (property): Column names in result order.

### `ArrowBatch`

Owned native columns; exported buffers remain valid after stream/pool close.

- **`num_rows`** (property): Rows in this batch.
- **`num_columns`** (property): Columns in this batch.
- **`nbytes`** (property): Bytes held by the batch's Arrow buffers.
- **`schema`** (property): Column names and Arrow types, including SQL metadata.

### `FirebirdConfig`

Immutable connection and pool settings; ``FirebirdConfig()`` reads ``FB_*`` and ``.env``.

Precedence per option: explicit argument > environment > ``.env`` file > default.
``database``, ``user`` and ``password`` have no default and must come from one
of these sources. Construction validates everything but never connects.
See the constructor parameters for meaning, limits and defaults.

Every option is listed in [configuration.md](configuration.md).

- **`from_env`** (method): Optional shortcut for a custom variable prefix; FirebirdConfig() already reads FB_*.

## Typing helpers

- **`DEFAULT`**
- **`DefaultTimeout`**: Type of :data:`DEFAULT`: "use the configured timeout" (``query_timeout`` or ``snapshot_timeout``).
- **`Timeout`**
- **`Params`**
- **`PoolStats`**: Snapshot of pool counters returned by ``Pool.stats()``.
- **`QueryTrace`**: Diagnostics for one pool query (``FirebirdConfig(diagnostics=True)``).
- **`PhaseTrace`**: One measured phase of a traced query.
- **`SessionInfo`**: Capabilities observed on a real attachment, returned by ``Pool.session_info()``.

## Errors

All errors derive from `FbFastError` and carry `phase`, `sqlstate`,
`native_codes` and `cleanup_errors`. See [errors.md](errors.md).

- **`FbFastError`**(Exception): Base class of every error raised by fbfast.
- **`AuthenticationError`**(FbFastError): The server rejected the user name or password (SQLSTATE 28000).
- **`CleanupError`**(FbFastError): Closing a cursor, transaction, statement or connection failed; the connection was discarded.
- **`ClientLibraryError`**(FbFastError): The Firebird client library could not be loaded or is not a supported 5.0.3+ client.
- **`ConfigurationError`**(FbFastError): Invalid, missing or unknown configuration value. Fix the configuration; do not retry.
- **`DataConversionError`**(FbFastError): A value could not be converted exactly between Firebird and Python.
- **`PoolError`**(FbFastError): Base class of pool lifecycle and capacity errors.
- **`QueryCancelledError`**(FbFastError): The operation was cancelled (task cancellation, stream close or group cancellation).
- **`QueryError`**(FbFastError): Firebird rejected or failed the statement. Inspect ``sqlstate`` and ``native_codes``.
- **`ReadOnlyViolationError`**(FbFastError): The server reported or the handshake detected a write attempt or a non read-only transaction.
- **`ResultLimitError`**(FbFastError): A materialized result or BLOB exceeded ``max_result_bytes``, ``max_result_rows`` or ``max_blob_bytes``.
- **`RoleNotActiveError`**(FbFastError): The requested role is not active for the session (missing grant or wrong name).
- **`UnsupportedFeatureError`**(FbFastError): The requested option or operation is outside what fbfast supports (e.g. ``read_only=False``).
- **`UnsupportedServerError`**(FbFastError): The server is not Firebird 5.0.x.
- **`UnsupportedStatementError`**(FbFastError): The SQL is not a single read-only SELECT/WITH query (DML, DDL, EXECUTE BLOCK...).
- **`UnsupportedTypeError`**(FbFastError): The result or a parameter uses a type fbfast does not convert (e.g. ARRAY).
- **`ForkSafetyError`**(PoolError): A pool, stream or snapshot created before ``fork()`` was used in the child. Create pools after forking.
- **`PoolAlreadyInitializedError`**(PoolError): A name is already reserved, including while opening or draining.
- **`PoolBusyError`**(PoolError): The waiting queue is full (``max_waiters``). Retrying later can succeed.
- **`PoolClosedError`**(PoolError): The pool is closing or closed, or its worker stopped. Create a new pool to continue.
- **`PoolNotInitializedError`**(PoolError): No ready pool is registered under the requested name.
- **`UsageError`**(FbFastError, RuntimeError): API misuse detected in Python, such as querying a snapshot or stream outside its ``with`` block.
- **`ArgumentError`**(FbFastError, ValueError, TypeError): Invalid argument value or type passed to an fbfast function.
- **`ConcurrentUseError`**(PoolBusyError): A snapshot or stream was used by two operations at once. Serialize its use; retrying will not help.
- **`DatabaseConnectionError`**(QueryError, ConnectionError): The server or network refused the connection or dropped it (SQLSTATE 08xxx).
- **`PoolTimeoutError`**(PoolError, TimeoutError): No connection became available within ``acquire_timeout``. Retrying later can succeed.
- **`QueryTimeoutError`**(QueryError, TimeoutError): The query deadline (``query_timeout``, ``timeout=`` or the snapshot deadline) expired.

## Deprecated (removed in 0.4.0)

`clear_statement_cache_sync`, `close_pool_sync`, `close_sync`, `init_pool_sync`, `snapshot_async`, `warmup_sync`: aliases kept for one release; they emit `DeprecationWarning`.
